TASK: The maintenance technician was closing an isolation valve on the overhead compressed air line above the assembly cell. The task was routine scheduled work. Stage of the task: planned maintenance. Method in effect: WI-330 Compressed Air Line Isolation. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method calls for the valve to be reached from the mobile platform, but the platform was in use elsewhere so a stepladder was used instead. Equipment involved: An 8 foot fiberglass stepladder, asset 20114, and the overhead air isolation valve. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: normal working order, nothing outstanding. The object handled weighed under 10 lb. Handling difficulty: small - fits in one hand. It was held one hand. PPE in use: safety glasses, steel toe boots and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The event was witnessed by at least one other person. Immediately before the event: standing on the third step of the stepladder with the left hand on the rail and the right arm extended up and out to the left toward the valve. Body position at the moment: on a ladder or step. At the moment of the event: the ladder shifted to the left as the reach extended past the side rail, the left foot came off the step, and the fall was taken onto the concrete landing on the right foot. Immediately after the event: the wrench was dropped clear, the technician sat on the floor unable to bear weight on the right foot, and a nearby operator called the supervisor.

MECHANISM: Footwear: slip resistant safety boots in good condition. Fall height: under 4 feet. Working surface and landing surface: An 8 foot fiberglass stepladder set on sealed concrete with one leg resting partly on a cable tray cover, landing on sealed concrete. Fall protection was not required for this work. It was not available at the location. It was not in use at the time. The fall was initiated when the ladder shifted to the left as the reach extended out past the side rail toward the valve. Point of contact: right ankle, rolling outward on landing. Force applied from below.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The mobile platform is normally used for this valve and was unavailable, and the cable tray cover made the ladder footing uneven. Conditions at the point of injury: restricted working space and an uneven or obstructed floor. Detail: The floor under the valve carries a cable tray cover about 2 inches proud, so the ladder could not be set level. The event occurred in the first hour of the shift. No overtime was being worked. It happened within the first few minutes. The maintenance technician had performed this task before. No known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The job could have waited for the mobile platform to become available, but the repair was scheduled for that morning.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: At the scene, a cold pack was applied. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notified: the supervisor and EHS. This happened immediately. Afterwards, the scene was left undisturbed for EHS and the area was barriered off. Work at the location stopped. The maintenance technician was sent to an emergency room for evaluation.
